correctness.rationale: Independent positive geometric lags, conditioned at birth n to G<=n, provide exact model coupling with disagreement probability q^n. Summed discrepancies give m q^(k+1)/(1-q). Outgoing and incoming crossings use disjoint source sets; their Bernoulli success probabilities are respectively q^(t-1) and q^(s-1)(1-q^L). Two independent tail couplings each cost m q^L/(1-q); exact algebra computes characteristic function, variance, negative covariances and spectral density. The checker passed 17,174 exact-rational assertions over finite cases; infinite claims rest on these summable probabilistic estimates.

value.rationale: This mathematically natural count quantifies the total degree imbalance on a long interval in the recent-neighbor graph. It exhibits a non-Gaussian boundary-only residual with explicit distribution, despite random local degrees, and a uniform finite-start total-variation rate in two scales; this quantifies finite-network uncertainty and identifies a conservation-driven mechanism absent from isolated-vertex degrees, maximum degrees, leaf CLTs and walk-recurrence results. The general qualitative hyperuniformity is known; value is specifically the explicit q-Bernoulli boundary law and quantitative finite-start comparison.
